data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: after
sections.summary: Used to show that one event happens at a later time than another; following in time or order.

senses.definition: used to introduce a clause describing an event that happens at a later time than the event in the main clause
examples: After the lesson ended, the students went to the library.

answers.answer: After she finished her homework, she went out with her friends.
After she finished her homework she went out, with her friends.
After she finished her homework, went out with her friends.
She went out after she will finish her homework.

sections.question: although
sections.summary: In spite of the fact that; used to introduce a contrast or something surprising.

senses.definition: used to introduce a clause that contains a fact which makes the main clause surprising or unexpected; in spite of the fact that
examples: Although the exam was hard, most students passed.

answers.answer: Although it was raining, they decided to continue the match.
Although it was raining but they decided to continue the match.
Although raining, they decided to continue the match.
They decided to continue the match although was raining.

sections.question: because
sections.summary: For the reason that; used to introduce a clause that gives a reason or explanation.

senses.definition: used to introduce a clause that gives the reason for what is stated in the main clause; for the reason that
examples: He wore a coat because the weather was cold.

answers.answer: She left early because she was feeling unwell.
She left early because of she was feeling unwell.
Because she was feeling unwell, so she left early.
She left early because was feeling unwell.

sections.question: before
sections.summary: Used to show that one event happens at an earlier time than another; earlier than.

senses.definition: used to introduce a clause describing an event that happens at an earlier time than the event in the main clause
examples: Make sure you turn off the lights before you leave.

answers.answer: Before you submit the form, check it carefully.
Before you submit the form check it carefully carefully.
Before submit the form, check it carefully.
You check it carefully before you will submit the form.

sections.question: even though
sections.summary: In spite of the fact that; used to introduce a strong contrast, emphasising that something is surprising.

synonyms: in spite of the fact that

senses.definition: used to introduce a clause that makes the main clause surprising or unexpected; a stronger form of 'although' used to emphasise the contrast
examples: She kept smiling even though she was clearly upset.

answers.answer: Even though he studied hard, he didn't pass the exam.
Even though he studied hard but he didn't pass the exam.
Even though studied hard, he didn't pass the exam.
He didn't pass the exam even though was studied hard.

sections.question: if
sections.summary: Used to introduce a condition; on the condition that something is or will be true.

senses.definition: used to introduce a clause expressing a condition; the main clause describes what happens when that condition is true or fulfilled
examples: If the weather is fine, we will have lunch outside.

answers.answer: If you need help, let me know.
If you will need help, let me know.
If need help, let me know.
Let me know if you would need help yesterday.
